q: How many legs does a spider have?
funFact: Insects have six legs — spiders are not insects at all.

q: What is a baby frog called?
funFact: Tadpoles start with no legs at all, then grow four.
Its wings beat about fifty times every second.

q: What do worms help make for gardens?
funFact: Worms eat old leaves and turn them into plant food.

q: In which season do most leaves fall off the trees?
funFact: That is exactly why it is called fall!

q: Which busy animal buries acorns all over the yard?
funFact: Squirrels forget some acorns — and those grow into new trees.
A big fluffy cloud can weigh as much as one hundred elephants.

q: Which part of a plant drinks water from the dirt?
funFact: Some tree roots reach wider than the tree is tall.

q: Which insect makes the honey we eat?
funFact: One bee makes only a tiny spoonful of honey in its whole life.

q: What do we call animals that sleep all winter?
funFact: Bears, chipmunks and even some frogs hibernate.
